clue.text: Race's competitors' old sex symbol

blocks.note: man is the human race, so the race's is man's
the field is everyone competing in a race

explanation.surface: A racing commentator recalls a glamour figure from among the runners of years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: Race is the human race, MAN, not a sporting event; the competitors are the FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Jayne Mansfield was a Hollywood actress promoted as a pin-up and bombshell in the 1950s.

clue.text: Time for tea or coffee

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
cha (char) is informal British for tea

explanation.surface: Someone at a café is told it is time to choose a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Time for tea reads as a phrase but splits into a moment and a word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, originally from the Yemeni port, now often flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: Drown in the endless suffering of bitter blow

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word next to it is dropped
suffering letters are in torment and twisted out of their usual shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word the without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed by misery as a harsh wind strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the north is cold, so a bitter blow is a strong chilly gust.

clue.text: Attached quickly with one end loose

indicators.note: letters set loose are free to fall into a different order

blocks.note: fast means quickly
the letters of one end rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was fixed in a hurry and one end has been left dangling.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten on to something is to attach yourself to it or seize on it firmly.

clue.text: Shout demand for alimony perhaps

blocks.note: alimony is paid to a former spouse, an ex
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: A divorce lawyer bellows a demand for maintenance payments.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as an ex's claim: the person who might demand alimony comes first, then the demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a verb meaning to shout.

clue.text: Crashed red mail truck

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is wrecked and mangled, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A red Post Office van has come off the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Daimler is a vehicle maker whose name is used for its lorries and trucks, as well as cars.

clue.text: Directions to appeal result

blocks.note: E and N, east and north, two compass points
to sue is to appeal to a court or to plead

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to lodge a legal appeal and get a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, so it works as the verb result.

clue.text: Girl lifted lid off problem

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means read upwards, so the word is turned around
taking something off a word removes those letters from it

blocks.note: taken as written, then read upwards
a dilemma is a difficult problem

explanation.surface: A girl solved a puzzle by prising the top off something.
explanation.walkthrough: DILEMMA begins with LID written backwards; removing it leaves the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a common female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Maybe common sight perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: the word that follows common in the phrase for practical good judgement
second meaning: one of the five faculties of perception, of which sight is an example

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works as a fill-in: common goes before the answer to make a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Common sense is everyday practical judgement, and sight is one of the bodily senses along with hearing and touch.

clue.text: The Spanish stitch woman's loose end in a different place

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
to sew is to stitch
her is the possessive for a woman
the final letter of loose

explanation.surface: A Spanish seamstress has a dangling thread that is somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means somewhere other than here, an adverb for in another location.

clue.text: See 25
Blocks out one afternoon for squirrels

indicators.note: the word for blocks sits outside, wrapping around the other piece

blocks.note: chunks are blocks or lumps
the Roman numeral for one
p.m. marks times in the afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a single afternoon to go squirrel-watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Blocks out looks like a verb meaning to reserve time, but blocks is a noun wrapped round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipmunks are small striped rodents belonging to the squirrel family.

clue.text: Can be done by a head with no tail. Very clever!

indicators.note: a word lacking its tail has its last letter cut away

blocks.note: taken as written
a chief is a head or leader
V is the abbreviation for very
able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: Praise for a tailless creature that has managed a feat with its head.
explanation.walkthrough: With no tail looks like it describes the creature, but it trims only the word for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Achievable means attainable or possible, so describes something that can be done.

clue.text: Echo cut out cat-call

indicators.note: the word for cut lies out around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: to mow is to cut grass
Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: An echo is silenced when the jeering from the crowd stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat-call wants to mean a jeer, but read literally it is the noise a cat makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Meow is the sound a cat makes, quite literally a cat's call.

clue.text: Boat called by outside conservation worker

indicators.note: the word for by goes outside, surrounding the other pieces

blocks.note: Noah's ark is a boat
rang means phoned or called
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A boat has been hailed by somebody standing outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A park ranger is employed to protect and manage the wildlife and land of a national park.

clue.text: Lions that come in a summer?

blocks.note: first meaning: a group of lions
second meaning: playful, as the proverb says this comes before a fall, and fall is autumn, so it comes in summer

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says this vice goes before a fall; in American English fall is autumn, so the season before it is summer. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective noun for a group of lions, and also the self-regard that the proverb warns about.

clue.text: Odd pureéd extract containing last word in poison

indicators.note: odd here means the letters in odd-numbered places, first, third and fifth
one word holds the other within it
the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of pureéd, accent dropped
juice is what is extracted from fruit
the final letter of word

explanation.surface: Instructions for a cook's purée, with a deadly twist at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To poison someone's mind is to prejudice it, turning them against something unfairly.

clue.text: Disorder made alarm spread

indicators.note: disorder means confusion, so the letters fall out of their arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Civil unrest caused panic to spread through the population.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread looks like the verb at the end of the sentence, but it is the noun: something spread on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve spread on bread or toast.

clue.text: Disease doesn't begin to describe the core of politics' powers

indicators.note: a word that fails to begin has lost its opening letter
the core of a word is its middle, so only the central letters are kept
to describe is literally to draw around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: rabies is a viral disease
the middle four letters of politics

explanation.surface: A comment that calling politics diseased does not go nearly far enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Doesn't begin to describe reads as an idiom for understatement, but each part is an instruction: lose the first letter, then wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilities are capacities or talents, so powers in the sense of things one is able to do.

clue.text: Start and finish of Final Score

blocks.note: the end is the final part
a score is counted in points

explanation.surface: It sounds like the opening and closing of the BBC results programme Final Score.
explanation.walkthrough: Final Score is a BBC television programme reading out the day's football results.
explanation.definitionFit: Endpoints are the two points at either end of a line or range, its start and finish.

clue.text: Points at badgers

blocks.note: first meaning: sharp tips, as of sewing or knitting tools
second meaning: pesters or provokes, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Badgers looks like the animals being pointed at, but it is a verb meaning nags.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are pointed instruments, and to needle someone is to irritate or harass them persistently.

clue.text: Discover America's going in one direction shortly

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter
one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: south is a compass direction
US is America, so America's is US's

explanation.surface: Find out whether the United States is heading in only one way soon.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortly suggests soon, but it trims the direction word by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss out is an informal phrasal verb for working something out or finding out about it.

clue.text: Cut held back by chef in kitchen

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the word boundaries
going back means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters across chef in kitchen

explanation.surface: A cut of meat has been set aside by the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut looks like a noun or the verb for slicing, but it defines a tool used to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a blade, and as a verb to knife is to cut or stab with one.

clue.text: State you got extra cash tips

indicators.note: tips are the ends of things, here the final letter of each word

blocks.note: the last letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A waiter declares that they received extra money in tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: A British governor for where they keep order

blocks.note: taken as written
B is an abbreviation for British
a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A colonial governor is appointed to maintain law and order.
explanation.walkthrough: Order here is not discipline but a religious order of monks or nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey houses a community of monks or nuns, who belong to a religious order.

clue.text: Rue passion that's mistaken for seduction

indicators.note: mistaken letters have gone wrong and need putting into the right order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Regret a passion that was misread as an attempt at seduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is a form of persuasion, coaxing someone into doing something by charm.

clue.text: Hill racer turns into rambler

indicators.note: a thing that turns round faces the other way, so read it backwards

blocks.note: Damon Hill is a former Formula One world champion racing driver

explanation.surface: Someone racing up a hill becomes a leisurely hill walker.
explanation.walkthrough: Hill is not a slope but the surname of the 1996 Formula One champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place with no fixed home, so is a rambler in the broad sense.

clue.text: Pictured messages after daughter stuck in traffic

indicators.note: something stuck in another thing is lodged inside it

blocks.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
traffic is made up of cars
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent sends pictures by text after a daughter is held up in a jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Postcards carry a picture on one side and a short message on the other.

clue.text: Fight grease and pass right weight test in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

blocks.note: oil is a lubricant or grease
to go is to pass, as in time goes
R is the abbreviation for right
body mass index, a measure of weight against height

explanation.surface: A retired boxer oils up and passes the weigh-in before a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused or bitter quarrel, a tangled fight or dispute.

clue.text: Dark Materials' original author

indicators.note: the original of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: grim means dark or bleak
the first letter of materials

explanation.surface: Who first wrote His Dark Materials? (It was Philip Pullman.)
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Philip Pullman's trilogy His Dark Materials, but Dark and Materials are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm, Jacob and Wilhelm, wrote down German folk tales, so a Grimm is an author.

clue.text: Say axis of empty planet's in place

indicators.note: an emptied word has its inside taken out, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, say
the y-axis of a graph
the first and last letters of planet

explanation.surface: Something like the axis of a deserted planet in space.
explanation.walkthrough: Empty looks like an adjective in its own right, but it acts on the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country, and a country is a place.

clue.text: Took off ruined Haiti dress without second thought

indicators.note: the second of a word is the letter in position two
without means lacking, so that letter is removed from the fodder
something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the second letter of thought

explanation.surface: Someone mocked a spoiled Caribbean garment without a second thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Without second thought reads as an idiom for doing something rashly, but it removes one letter from the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or parody them, which is what satirising does.
